findings.description: _read_all returns {} on any OSError or ValueError. If the session file exists but cannot be read (transient I/O error, permissions, a locked file), save(), delete() or take_by_refresh() call _read_all, get an empty dict, and then _write_all replaces the real file with a file containing only the new record. Every other user's session is lost and those users are logged out. A missing file should be treated as empty, but other read errors should surface as StoreError.
findings.suggestion: Return {} only when the file does not exist (FileNotFoundError). Wrap other OSError and ValueError/KeyError/TypeError from parsing in StoreError so writers abort instead of overwriting the file.
findings.title: Read failure is treated as an empty store, so the next write erases all sessions

findings.description: change_password calls sign_out_everywhere, which logs a warning and continues when store.delete raises StoreError. The caller gets a count that is lower than the number of sessions, but nothing signals failure. A session the attacker holds can survive a password change that was meant to end every session, and the user believes they are signed out everywhere.
findings.suggestion: Do not swallow StoreError in sign_out_everywhere when called from change_password. Propagate the error, or retry and fail the password change, so the caller knows not all sessions were revoked.
findings.title: Failed revocation during password change leaves sessions alive

findings.description: SessionManager's ttl parameter is gone and a required store argument was inserted as the second positional parameter. Callers that pass ttl by keyword get a TypeError, and callers that pass ttl positionally now pass it as the store. login() also returns IssuedSession instead of Session, which no longer has a token field, and the default lifetime drops from 12 hours to a 30-minute access token with no refresh call in the old clients, so those clients are logged out after 30 minutes.
findings.suggestion: Keep ttl working as an alias for access_ttl, make store a keyword argument with a default, and document the migration for clients that must call refresh().
findings.title: Constructor signature and session model changed for existing callers

findings.description: FileSessionStore reads and rewrites the full JSON file on each delete. sign_out_everywhere and purge_expired call all() and then delete() for each matching record, so ending N sessions costs N full reads and writes. With a large number of live sessions this becomes slow and blocks other requests on the lock.
findings.suggestion: Add a batch delete method to the store protocol that removes several access hashes in one read and one write, and use it from sign_out_everywhere and purge_expired.
findings.title: Whole-file rewrite on every change makes sign-out and purge quadratic
